title: Renew a library loan
description: A library loan has an item title, a due day (a day number) and a count of renewals already used. Write renew_loan, which takes the loan and today's day number and returns the renewed loan or an error. A renewal moves the due day 14 days later than the current due day (not later than today) and raises the renewal count by one; the title is unchanged. Checks happen in this order, and the first failing one decides the result: a loan that is past due, meaning today is after the due day, gives the error "overdue by " followed by the number of days past due and " days" (for example "overdue by 1 days"); a loan with two or more renewals already used gives "renewal limit reached for " followed by the item title; a renewal is only allowed in the last 3 days before the due day, so if today is more than 3 days before the due day the error is "too early: renew from day " followed by the first day on which renewal is allowed. Renewing on the due day itself is allowed.
notes: Level 1: one record, three ordered checks, a computed message. Pitfalls: the new due day is old due day + 14, not today + 14; the overdue check comes before the limit check, and the limit check before the too-early check; the due day itself is not overdue; the earliest renewal day is due_day - 3.
